title: DCPSC Order No. 23132 (2026-07-29) — The Public Service Commission of the District of Columbia, in Formal Case No. 1178, by Order No. 23132, dated July 29, 2026, extended the timeline for the Commi
description: The Public Service Commission of the District of Columbia, in Formal Case No. 1178, by Order No. 23132, dated July 29, 2026, extended the timeline for the Commission’s staff to hold the next technical conference in this proceeding. The Commission’s staff is directed to hold the next technical conference by September 14, 2026.
text:
PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION OF THE DISTRICT OF COLUMBIA 
1325 G STREET, N.W., SUITE 800 
WASHINGTON, D.C. 20005 

ORDER 
July 29, 2026 

FORMAL CASE NO. 1178, IN THE MATTER OF PETITION FOR INVESTIGATION 
INTO WASHINGTON GAS LIGHT COMPANY’S SYSTEM LEAK REDUCTION 
PRACTICES, Order No. 23132 

I. 
INTRODUCTION 

1. 
By this Order, the Public Service Commission of the District of Columbia 
(“Commission”) extends the timeline for the Commission staff to hold the next technical 
conference in Formal Case No. 1178, set by Order No. 22890. 

II. 
BACKGROUND 

2. 
On June 30, 2026, the Commission issued Order No. 22890, which directed 
Commission staff to continue the proceedings in Formal Case No. 1178 and schedule a technical 
conference within forty-five (45) days of the Order.1 The 45-day period expires August 14, 2026. 
Order No. 22890 also specified that Washington Gas Light Company (“WGL”) provide a 
presentation at the technical conference that addressed its current capabilities regarding the 
following: (1) the availability and timeliness of data and applications for representing transient and 
changing leak data in geospatial information systems (“GIS”); (2) how to balance providing 
information on addressed leaks or issues compared to open leaks or issues and how rapidly that 
information can be available and updated, (3) how advanced leak detection can be incorporated 
into GIS or graphics displaying leaks; (4) how information currently contained in LIDAROC 
differs from information required to create quarterly or annually updated leak maps; and (5) 
identification and explanation of the specific critical energy infrastructure information constraints 
involved in leak mapping pursuant to the Commission’s authority and rules.2 

III. 
DECISION 

3. 
The Commission notes that the technical conference has not yet occurred and only 
a few business days remain before the August 14 deadline. While the Commission Staff diligently 
attempted to schedule a technical conference as directed by Order No. 22890, due to conflicting 
summer schedules and limited availability of all parties involved in this proceeding, it has become 
necessary to extend the deadline for the technical conference. Therefore, the Commission extends 
the deadline to hold the next Formal Case No. 1178 technical conference by thirty (30) days. The 
Commission staff is directed to hold the next technical conference for Formal Case No. 1178 by

4.
